Firmware upgrade, boot partition and reports

Pre-flight one appliance, flash a FortiWeb to a new firmware from the library inside an approved change window, roll back with Boot Partition, and read the before/after report of every flash.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsappliances.apply appliances.view
📍 WhereAppliances → (device) → Appliance Actions → Upgrade Prep / Upgrade / Boot Partition / Firmware Reports

What is it?#

Four pages on an appliance cover a firmware change of one device:

  • Upgrade Prep — a read-only pre-flight: configuration backup, SSH health battery, maintenance-permission check and a test of every published service. Every run is recorded.
  • Upgrade — flashes a FortiWeb with an image from the Firmware library. A dry run is always allowed; a live flash only inside an approved change request's window.
  • Boot Partition — rolls a FortiWeb back to an older image (a downgrade), targeting the alternate firmware partition. It is the emergency path: no change request is needed, but a live flash must be acknowledged as bypassing change control.
  • Firmware Reports — the before/after report of every upgrade and boot-partition flash.

To upgrade several appliances in one maintenance window, use Upgrade Flow, which builds on the same pre-flight.

What does it do?#

  • Upgrade Prep (FortiWeb and FortiADC) stores a backup in the vault, captures the health battery over SSH, reads whether the account has maintenance permission, probes every published service over HTTP and records the affected services. Nothing on the device changes.
  • Upgrade (FortiWeb):
  • reads the running firmware live and stores it on the appliance;
  • offers the library upgrade images that match the appliance's product and platform, newest first (install images are never offered);
  • shows the change-control status and the latest pre-flight;
  • shows Upgrade Advisory — release-notes review for the selected image (see Release notes; called Scout until 2026-10-14);
  • runs the flash as a background job with a full runbook (below);
  • points to Upgrade Flow for flashing in a planned maintenance window.
  • Boot Partition (FortiWeb) labels each image as [↓ rollback], [↑ upgrade], [= current] or [?] against the running version, pre-selects the newest older image, and flashes it to the alternate partition, answering the device's downgrade and maturity confirmations.
  • Firmware Reports lists every flash report with filters for All, Upgrades and Boot Partition, counters (Total Reports, Upgrades, Boot Partition, Need Attention) and a search box.

Requirements#

  • Upgrade and Boot Partition: a FortiWeb. FortiADC exposes no REST firmware or partition endpoint, so these stay FortiWeb-only.
  • At least one matching upgrade image in the Firmware library (same product; platform matching or universal).
  • The device account must have maintenance permission; a flash is refused otherwise.
  • For a live Upgrade: a change request for the action upgrade that names this appliance, is approved, scheduled or in progress, and whose window is open now.
  • On a multi-ADOM FortiWeb, these pages live on the row that owns the device; other rows are redirected there.

Permissions#

Action Permission
Upgrade Prep — open, run, read a recorded run appliances.apply
Upgrade — open, dry run, live flash, Upgrade Advisory appliances.apply — plus an open change window for a live flash
Boot Partition — open, dry run, live flash appliances.apply, without the change-window requirement; a live flash needs the change-control bypass acknowledgement
Firmware Reports — the buttons on the appliance page and the appliance list, and the pages themselves appliances.view. The list and each report cover only appliances visible to you.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: Upgrade, Boot Partition and Upgrade Prep require appliances.apply, and Firmware Reports require appliances.view and show only reports of devices visible to you. The Schedule for later card is gone (use Upgrade Flow), install images are no longer offered, and a live Boot Partition flash needs an acknowledgement that it bypasses change control.

🔑Permission — Without the permission

Without appliances.apply the Upgrade Prep button is hidden and the URLs of all three pages answer 403 Forbidden. The Upgrade and Boot Partition buttons are drawn for users with any edit permission; without appliances.apply they lead to 403 Forbidden.

How to use#

1. Run Upgrade Prep#

  1. On the appliance page click Upgrade Prep.
  2. Keep or clear Config backup, Health battery (SSH) and Service validation.
  3. Click Run preparation. The result shows Firmware, Maintenance permission, Backup, Services validated, the Service validation table, the Health battery (SSH) output and Affected services captured with this run.
  4. The run is added to Recorded pre-flight runs (10 most recent) with its verdict (passed or not clean). View result reopens a recorded run; a recorded run is labelled as such so it is never mistaken for a fresh one.
  5. To raise the change request a live upgrade needs, click Raise change request on the run, or Full upgrade flow at the top of the page. Both open Upgrade Flow with this appliance (and run) selected.

2. Validate the image (dry run)#

  1. Click Upgrade. The page warns that a live upgrade reboots the appliance.
  2. Under Apply now, the Firmware image (auto-detected from repository) list pre-selects the newest matching image. Each entry shows version, build, platform, size and checksum prefix.
  3. Leave Dry run (validate the image only — nothing is sent) ticked. Tick Ask the Upgrade Advisory to review the release notes for this version if you want the review (disabled when Path Diagnostics is switched off for the site: the page then says Turn on Path Diagnostics in Settings → Path Diagnostics to see the Upgrade Advisory.).
  4. Click Validate / Accept. A job Validate 7.6.8 for fweb-01 checks the image's checksum and the maintenance permission, and reports DRY-RUN — would upload … to fweb-01 … and reboot. No image was sent.

3. Flash for real#

  1. Check the change-control box at the top. It must read Authorised by CR-… with the window; otherwise it reads Live upgrade is blocked. with the reason.
  2. Untick Dry run. Tick Confirm maturity change (Mature↔Feature, e.g. 7.6→8.0) when crossing between a Mature and a Feature release.
  3. Type the appliance name in Type the appliance name fweb-01 to authorise the live reboot:.
  4. Click Validate / Accept. The job Upgrade fweb-01 → 7.6.8 runs in the background and shows each step:
  1. 1Pre-flightSafety backup into the vault, SSH health battery, baseline of the published services
  2. 2Upload and flashThe image is uploaded and the device asked to install it
  3. 3RebootSATOM watches the device go down and come back
  4. 4Post-flightServices and health battery tested again and compared with the baseline
  5. 5RecordNew firmware stored on the appliance; before/after report written
  6. 6RediscoverA full rediscovery refreshes SATOM's view of the device
  1. You get a notification Upgrade complete: fweb-01 → 7.6.8 linking to the report. The change request moves to in progress when the job starts and is closed with the job's real outcome.

Upgrade in a maintenance window#

The Upgrade page flashes now, inside an approved change request. To plan the flash for a window, follow the link at the bottom of the page: To flash in a maintenance window, use Upgrade Flow. Upgrade Flow raises the change request with its window, and schedules the upgrade once it is approved.

Scheduled upgrade entries created by earlier releases from this page are left as they are under Scheduled actions.

Roll back with Boot Partition#

  1. Click Boot Partition on the appliance page. The page warns that a downgrade can reset the configuration, especially across a major branch, and to take a backup first. A second banner reads Emergency path — no change request.
  2. Under Roll back now, the newest image older than the running version is pre-selected. If no older image exists, a note says there is nothing to roll back to.
  3. Dry run first, then untick Dry run.
  4. Tick I understand this live flash bypasses change control (no change request) and is audited, type the appliance name and click Validate / Roll back.
  5. The live job targets the alternate partition and confirms the downgrade and maturity prompts itself. It runs the same pre-flight, reboot watch, post-flight, report and rediscovery as an upgrade.

❗Important — Not gated by change control

Unlike Upgrade and HA failover, a live Boot Partition flash does not require an approved change request, so it can roll a device back when a change has gone wrong. That is why it asks for the explicit acknowledgement, and why every attempt — refused, started, failed or successful — is written to the audit log. Plan it through your change process whenever you can.

Read the reports#

Click Firmware Reports on the appliance page or at the top of the appliance list. The list holds the reports of the appliances you can see in the current ADOM. Each row shows the machine, direction, verdict and downtime; open a row for the full before/after page with the service validation and the SSH battery.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Config backup / Health battery (SSH) / Service validation Parts of the pre-flight to run — all ticked
Firmware image A compatible library image Yes 7.6.8 (build 1128) — Virtual Machine
Dry run Validate only — ticked by default
Ask the Upgrade Advisory to review the release notes Add the Upgrade Advisory's review to the run No ticked
Confirm maturity change Answer the device's Mature↔Feature confirmation When crossing ticked
Type the appliance name Required for a live flash Live only fweb-01
I understand this live flash bypasses change control Boot Partition only: acknowledgement for a live flash Live only ticked

Example#

🧪Example — Upgrading one FortiWeb on a Saturday night

  1. Thursday: Upgrade Prep on fweb-01 → passed. Raise change request → Upgrade Flow; window Saturday 22:00–23:00; approved Friday.
  2. Saturday 22:05: Upgrade, banner Authorised by CR-…. Dry run with the Upgrade Advisory: verdict caution, one known issue noted.
  3. Live run with the typed name. 14 minutes later: fweb-01 is back online on FortiWeb-VM 7.6.8 (was 7.6.4) · services 12/12 reachable. Recovered in 412s. Pre-upgrade backup: … Full before/after report available. Rediscovery: …
  4. The change request closes as successful.

Result#

  • A recorded pre-flight run per Run preparation (audit appliance.upgrade_prep).
  • Per flash: a job, a safety backup in the vault, the new firmware on the appliance, a before/after report, a fresh rediscovery snapshot and a bell notification.
  • Audit entries: appliance.upgrade_scout (when the Upgrade Advisory warns), appliance.upgrade_refused, appliance.upgrade.complete, appliance.upgrade.failed, appliance.downgrade.complete, appliance.downgrade.failed, and appliance.downgrade for a live Boot Partition attempt (outcome refused, started, success or failure, with the change-control bypass recorded).

Troubleshooting#

"Live upgrade refused — change control: no approved change request names this appliance for upgrade. Run the upgrade preparation, raise a change request from it, get it approved, and flash inside its window."#

Possible causes — No approved change for upgrade names this appliance, or its window is not open (the message names the closest change and why).

Solution — Raise the change from Upgrade Prep (Raise change request), get it approved, and flash inside the window. Dry runs keep working meanwhile.

"A live boot-partition flash bypasses change control. Tick the acknowledgement to proceed."#

Possible causes — A live Boot Partition flash was submitted without the acknowledgement. Nothing was sent; the refusal is audited.

Solution — Tick I understand this live flash bypasses change control (no change request) and is audited and run again.

"Type the exact appliance name to authorise the live upgrade."#

Solution — Type the name exactly as in the page title.

"fweb-01 staged the image but needs MATURITY confirmation (confirm_maturity_M_to_F) — not installed, no reboot."#

Solution — Run again with Confirm maturity change ticked.

"satom-api lacks maintenance permission on fweb-01"#

Possible causes — The device account's admin profile has no maintenance permission.

Solution — Grant it on the device, then run the dry run again (the Maintenance permission line shows the result).

"fweb-01 did not come back online within the wait window (~900s). The flash may still be in progress — check the console."#

Solution — Check the device's console. When it is back, run a Rediscovery.

"fweb-01 never rebooted and is still on 7.6.4. The image was uploaded but NOT installed …"#

Possible causes — The device did not accept this image or upgrade path.

Solution — Check the vendor upgrade path (the Upgrade Advisory shows the hop path), then flash the intermediate image first.

"No firmware image in the repository matches this appliance (fortiweb / FortiWeb 600F)."#

Solution — Upload the image in the Firmware library with the right product and platform, and Image type Upgrade.

"Firmware file problem: …" / "sha256 mismatch …"#

Possible causes — The stored image is missing or changed on disk.

Solution — Delete and re-upload the image.

Advanced#

Advanced The job and the change request

The flash runs as a background job that cannot be cancelled once started. When the job was authorised by a change request, the change is started when the job starts and finished with the job's final status — success maps to ok, anything else to that status. Without JavaScript the page falls back to a synchronous flash, which does not run the pre-flight, reboot watch or report.

Advanced Image list

The Upgrade and Boot Partition pickers list the library images of the appliance's product whose platform fits and whose type is Upgrade. Install images (.qcow2, .ova and the like) build a new machine and are never offered for a flash.

Advanced Reports on disk

Each report is a self-contained page stored on the node per job, so it survives after the job record expires.
